answer: A newcomer earns standing by tending a cedar sapling on a ridge, logging it through a crystal prism in the canopy — on three gale days, photographs the noon spectrum — timestamp and wind reading, witnessed by a neighbour. Two wardens verify the log in six days, checking spectra against the prism's refraction table and wind against ridge records. A copied photo, a spectrum never cast, or a gale never felt voids the season, burns the 55-credit stake, bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 55 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 saplings and 3,000 spectra checked against a real crystal.
